conservation-of-mechanical-energy.title: Conservation of Mechanical Energy
conservation-of-mechanical-energy.interpretation: Total mechanical energy is preserved in systems where all forces are conservative. This represents the sum of the system's kinetic energy and its potential energy configuration.
conservation-of-mechanical-energy.symmetry_origin: According to Noether's Theorem, this conservation law is the direct consequence of time translation symmetry. If the Lagrangian is independent of absolute time, energy is an invariant.
conservation-of-mechanical-energy.limits_and_boundary: Broken in non-conservative systems where energy is dissipated as heat (Entropy). In General Relativity, global conservation is complicated by the expansion of the spacetime manifold.

linear-eigenvalue-equation-ident-aab898b.symmetry_origin: The invariance of specific directions (principal axes) under a linear transformation.
linear-eigenvalue-equation-ident-aab898b.limits_and_boundary: Identifies the fundamental 'Modes' or 'States' of a physical system, such as normal modes of oscillation or energy eigenstates in quantum mechanics.

probability-of-origin-d0baa24d.title: Phase Space Volume Probability of Cosmic Origin
probability-of-origin-d0baa24d.interpretation: Probability of Origin: The calculated statistical weight of the universe's initial state, demonstrating the extreme fine-tuning required for an arrow of time.
probability-of-origin-d0baa24d.symmetry_origin: Under the Liouville theorem, phase space volume is conserved under Hamiltonian flow, meaning the extreme low entropy of the start must be set as an initial boundary condition.
probability-of-origin-d0baa24d.limits_and_boundary: In the limit where the initial state entropy approaches the maximum possible entropy ($S_{\mathrm{init}} \to S_{\mathrm{max}}$), the probability $P_{\mathrm{origin}} \to 1$, which represents a generic, non-fine-tuned universe in thermal equilibrium.
